subject.title: feat(slack): support running as a real Slack user (user identity)

question: Should this Slack user-identity mode merge before its user-scoped DM/group-DM event path is demonstrated in a live workspace?
rationale: Slack's documentation makes the design plausible, but only a maintainer can accept the operational and credential-boundary risk of shipping the new mode without observing its central user flow.

options.title: Require live proof first
options.body: Fix the slash-command identity collision and add redacted live DM/group-DM send-and-receive evidence before merging.

options.title: Accept the opt-in risk
options.body: Merge after the command fix while explicitly accepting that live user-scoped delivery remains a post-merge validation obligation.

options.title: Pause user identity
options.body: Keep the bundled Slack plugin bot-only until the companion-app approach has stronger field validation or an external plugin proves it.

recommendation.title: Require live proof first
recommendation.body: Fix the slash-command identity collision and add redacted live DM/group-DM send-and-receive evidence before merging.

likelyOwner.reason: This person authored the feature's design and implementation and is the strongest evidence-backed owner for accepting or rejecting the proof gap.
